rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to tune selectivity in either direction.

Change only gradient duration to determine whether the critical cluster responds to a shallower slope. The initial last-peak time suggests this run should remain close to the 10-minute scoring threshold.

Trim the gradient window while keeping nearly the same slope as the fully resolved second run. Starting at higher organic should bring the last peak below 10 minutes while largely preserving the critical-pair resolution.

Raise the starting organic fraction one step, which also makes the gradient slightly shallower. This should improve the critical pair’s resolution while moving the elution window earlier, preserving a last-peak time below 10 minutes.

Lower the endpoint one step to make the gradient shallower without changing the starting conditions. This should lift the critical pair above R = 1.5 while using the available 0.92-minute margin before the time penalty begins.
Injection 5 has reached the maximum CRF; retain it as the benchmark. Increase temperature one step to seek a shorter fully resolved separation and measure the critical pair’s temperature sensitivity.

The critical pair converges strongly with increasing temperature, suggesting it may separate again after an elution-order reversal. Test 55 C for a faster fully resolved separation, while monitoring the other narrowing gaps and retaining injection 5 as the maximum-score benchmark.

Make the 55 C gradient slightly shallower to improve the newly critical pair at R = 1.41. The 1.46-minute margin below the time threshold allows some additional retention while seeking another fully resolved, maximum-score method.

Shift both gradient endpoints upward one step, preserving the slope while moving elution earlier. Test whether this shortens the fully resolved separation without compromising the early peaks or either critical pair.

Lower the starting organic fraction to recover selectivity in the early critical pair, while shortening and steepening the gradient to reduce the last-peak time. This tests a faster alternative to injection 8, which remains the shortest fully resolved method observed.

Shorten the fastest fully resolved method by one duration step to test its resolution limit. Keeping the solvent window and temperature fixed will isolate the effect of gradient steepness on both critical pairs.

Reduce the endpoint to give a slope between injections 10 and 11, targeting recovery of the critical pair to R ≥ 1.5. This should retain most of the time savings from the shorter gradient while keeping the final peak inside the gradient.

Test whether lowering the starting organic fraction improves the critical early pair enough to tolerate a steeper gradient. This could shorten the separation relative to injection 12 while preserving full resolution; monitor the later critical pair, whose margin is also small.

With the maximum CRF already secured, test a faster high-temperature regime where the early critical pair may separate after an elution-order reversal. Keep the low starting organic fraction to retain the early peaks while assessing whether the steeper gradient preserves sufficient resolution.

Test a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower slope than injection 14 to spread the compressed middle cluster. At 60 C, the shifted solvent window may also strengthen separation of the reversed early critical pair, potentially giving full resolution in a substantially shorter run.

Shorten injection 15 to test whether a steeper gradient separates the reversed critical pair at 60 C. The neighboring pair has R = 2.49, providing some room for compression while pursuing a much faster fully resolved method.

Explore lower-temperature selectivity by changing only temperature from the original scouting method. This may resolve the middle cluster through a different elution order; the original 7.16-minute last peak leaves room for increased retention before the time penalty.

Test intermediate low-temperature selectivity with a moderately steep gradient, avoiding the severe clustering seen at 25 C. This explores whether the critical middle pairs can resolve in a faster regime than the current shortest fully resolved method.

Test whether a steep gradient at 45 C separates the middle cluster after reversal of the critical pair, without the early-pair convergence seen at 60 C. This explores a substantially faster regime while retaining the established maximum-score methods as benchmarks.

Return to the shortest fully resolved method, injection 13, and raise its endpoint one step to test the speed limit locally. This isolates a small slope increase; retain injection 13 if either critical pair drops below R = 1.5.

The faster neighboring method lost full resolution, so prioritize additional resolution margin while retaining CRF = 1.000. Slightly flatten injection 10’s gradient to improve its early critical pair and check whether the later pair remains fully resolved, with ample room below 10 minutes.

Shift injection 5’s solvent window upward while preserving its slope to test a shorter separation at 40 C. The lower temperature should retain the early peaks better than the unsuccessful high-starting-organic trial at 55 C, though the middle critical pair must be checked.

Flatten injection 22’s gradient to recover the critical pair’s resolution while preserving its improved early elution. The last peak should remain near but below 10 minutes, offering another potential maximum-score method without repeating a previous setting.

Trim the fastest fully resolved method’s endpoint and duration while preserving its exact gradient slope. Its last peak eluted near organic fraction 0.57, so this endpoint should preserve the separation while completing the programmed gradient two minutes earlier.

Use the final injection to refine the fully resolved injection 8 with a slightly shallower slope and a shorter programmed gradient. This should improve its minimum resolution while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes; injection 24 remains the shortest demonstrated maximum-score separation.
